newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Partner or merger seen for Philippine sugar mill.
newsitem.headline: Partner or merger seen for Philippine sugar mill.

text.p: A week after Victorias Milling Co was given some breathing space for repaying $168 million in debt, analysts on Wednesday were debating whether the Philippines' largest sugar mill might attract a buyer.
Victorias shares hit an all-time low of 2.80 pesos on Friday -- a day after the announcement of its massive debt problems. But there has been steady buying since.
On Wednesday, traders said talk of a takeover or strategic partner combined with a technical rebound to boost the share price to a close of 4.20 pesos.

On March 6, Victorias secured a 90-day moratorium on debt principal repayments from 32 local and foreign banks. Its cash shortfall stemmed from a sharp drop in sugar prices and debt-funded expansions, analysts said.
Victorias officials were not available for comment on the speculation about a takeover.
"They are looking for a strategic partner," said Saturnino Mejia, research head at Guoco Securities. "There is speculation that there might be a takeover."
Among the companies mentioned as possible partners or takeover suitors are sugar mill Jardine Davies and businessmen John Gokongwei and Lucio Tan.
Gokongwei runs a diversified group while Tan is a tobacco tycoon with interests in brewing and the airline business.
None of the three could be reached for comment on Wednesday.
"What will compel (a buyer) is the breakup value, which is dirt cheap," said Gina Manzano, an investment analyst at Asia Equity. She estimated book value at around 17 pesos per share.

Noel Reyes, head of research at Anscor Hagedorn Securities, said Jardine Davies appeared to be interested in an equity purchase and could be preparing a bid in conjunction with a consortium of smaller players.

He said he suspected any stake buyer would end up paying at least two billion pesos ($76 million), but added that the outcome would hinge on an ongoing audit of the company, which creditors hope will be wrapped up within a month.
"Based on the audit, those that have expressed an interest (in buying stock) will decide whether to go for it or not," he said.
Peter Verhoeven, group country head for Deutsche Bank, which heads the group of seven foreign bank creditors, said it was "too early" to comment on what options the creditors would pick.
Asked if the banks would be consulted on any takeover or equity bids that may emerge, Verhoeven told Reuters: "I think we would all want to play a role (in this)."

The creditor group, which formed a committee to seek a recovery plan, has been meeting daily to seek a solution. Victorias has told its lenders it has enough funds to pay an interest payment due on March 14.

One major creditor, the Bank of the Philippine Islands (BPI), sought to reassure shareholders on Tuesday by saying the 450 million pesos debt to Victorias's parent company represented just half a percent of BPI total loans and two percent of its capital. ($1=26.30)
